problem: From any given starting point, construct a nonzero segment equal to a given nonzero segment, including when the starting point coincides with an input endpoint.
proof_idea: Choose the endpoint by adding the positive square root of the input squared length to the starting point's first coordinate. Verify its distance, distinctness and membership in the circle with that center and radius. Euclid instead uses an equilateral triangle, extensions, circles and subtraction of equal segments; that original proof is recorded but not yet replayed.
litex_code:
thm proposition_2:
    ? forall a, b, c cart(R, R):
        b != c
        =>:
            exist d cart(R, R) st {a != d, $geometry::main::are_segments_congruent(a, d, b, c)}
    release thm geometry::main::distance_sq_positive_of_ne(b, c)
    have radius R+ = sqrt(geometry::main::distance_sq(b, c))
    sqrt(geometry::main::distance_sq(b, c))^2 = geometry::main::distance_sq(b, c)
    radius^2 = sqrt(geometry::main::distance_sq(b, c))^2 = geometry::main::distance_sq(b, c)
    have endpoint cart(R, R) = (a(1) + radius, a(2))
    endpoint(1) = a(1) + radius
    endpoint(2) = a(2)
    release thm geometry::main::distance_sq_coordinate_formula(a, endpoint)
    geometry::main::distance_sq(a, endpoint) = (endpoint(1) - a(1))^2 + (endpoint(2) - a(2))^2 = ((a(1) + radius) - a(1))^2 + (a(2) - a(2))^2 = radius^2 = geometry::main::distance_sq(b, c)
    by contra:
        ? a != endpoint
        a = endpoint
        a(1) = endpoint(1)
        a(1) = endpoint(1) = a(1) + radius
        radius = (a(1) + radius) - a(1) = endpoint(1) - a(1) = a(1) - a(1) = 0
        impossible radius > 0
    by def $geometry::main::are_segments_congruent(a, endpoint, b, c)
    release obj def geometry::main::circle
    geometry::main::distance_sq(a, endpoint) = radius * radius
    endpoint $in geometry::main::circle(a, radius)
    witness exist d cart(R, R) st {a != d, $geometry::main::are_segments_congruent(a, d, b, c)} from endpoint
